white_space:
Caveat on confidence: the WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before any of my searches ran, so the competitor check is thinner than requested. It rests on direct fetches of about 15 vendor and trade-publication pages plus Becker's ASC on-site search result pages. The Becker's article bodies returned 403. Crunchbase, Reddit and Product Hunt were not reachable. I found no dedicated competitor doing what this idea describes, and I could not check the many small RCM and consulting shops that a live web search would surface. I also could not confirm Cloudmed/R1 or Experian Contract Manager features (the R1 URL 404'd). Both are plausible incumbents with contract modeling.

What looks unserved, and is specific: (1) a contingency service focused only on the implant/device carve-out. It would join the OR implant log (manufacturer, catalog and lot numbers) to the AP vendor invoice, then to the payer contract carve-out clause, then to the 835 line. None of the general underpayment vendors above advertise this. (2) The buyer is the physician-owned spine/ortho ASC. Enterprise tools like Sift, FinThrive and Aspirion are aimed at health systems. (3) The claim-side fix is assembling the invoice attachment per payer rules and filing a corrected claim inside timely-filing limits. General contract-modeling tools mostly stop at flagging a variance.

Risks to the premise:
- 'Nobody connects them' is overstated. Becker's ran 'ASC Implant Carve-Outs: Opportunities, Challenges & 4 Best Practices' in 2014, so ASC operators know carve-outs exist (https://www.beckersasc.com/asc-coding-billing-and-collections/asc-implant-carve-outs-opportunities-challenges-4-best-practices/). ASC-specialist billers such as SIS/Surgical Notes, National Medical Billing Services and Nimble probably submit implant invoices as routine, so the addressable leakage may sit mostly in ASCs with weak or outsourced generalist billing.
- Any player with a contingency model and payer-contract modeling could add this quickly. Aspirion's ContractIQ is the most obvious.
- Medicare does not carve out implants in the ASC setting, so this is a commercial-contract play only. Each payer contract must be read individually, which limits how far it scales.
- I could not verify the CY2026 IPO-list phase-out and ASC list additions cited in the idea's why-now. CMS's page confirms only that a CY2026 ASC final rule (CMS-1834-FC) exists.
evidence_of_demand:
Indirect only. I found no direct evidence (forum complaints, RFPs or pricing pages) that ASCs pay a third party to recover unbilled implant carve-outs.

Supportive signals from Becker's ASC, snippets only because the article bodies returned 403:
- 'ASCs' implant cost problem' (Mar 12, 2026): 'For many ASCs, implants have become a difficult expense to manage, often requiring large upfront payments while reimbursement remains inconsistent.' https://www.beckersasc.com/asc-coding-billing-and-collections/ascs-implant-cost-problem/
- 'The burden of implant costs: 10 things ASCs need to know' (Feb 12, 2025): 'High costs of surgical implants have been identified as a profitability-killer for ASCs.' https://www.beckersasc.com/asc-coding-billing-and-collections/the-burden-of-implant-costs-10-things-ascs-need-to-know/
- 'The payer terms ASCs can't miss' (Jul 2026): 'payer talks this year came down to fine print, implant costs and case-level cost data.' https://www.beckersasc.com/asc-coding-billing-and-collections/the-payer-terms-ascs-cant-miss/
- Nimble Solutions sponsored content: 'ASCs face heightened revenue and cash flow risk... particularly with implant-and device heavy procedures.' https://www.beckersasc.com/asc-transactions-and-valuation-issues/unlocking-cash-flow-3-proven-ar-strategies-every-asc-needs/
- Becker's search for 'implant carve-out' returns 219 results and 'implant billing vendor' returns 187, so the topic is heavily covered.

There is also existing spend on adjacent contingency recovery: Aspirion reports $6B+ in client recoveries and sells on a contingency model (https://www.aspirion.com). That shows buyers accept contingency recovery in general, not for this niche.

The other demand evidence, that unbilled carve-outs are large and invisible, comes only from the idea file and is unverified. It needs the free 90-day lookback audits to prove.
sharper_angle:
Don't pitch 'revenue cycle recovery'. Pitch a narrow implant-to-cash reconciliation for spine and ortho ASCs, sold as a contingency lookback that turns into a prospective pre-bill check.

1. Start with the join no one else does: OR implant log (lot and catalog numbers) to vendor invoice to payer carve-out clause to 835 line. Compute an expected carve-out payment per case, at invoice cost plus the contract's markup.
2. Run the first 5-10 audits by hand with a coder, on payers whose contracts explicitly carve out implants. That yields a real dollar figure per case as sales proof.
3. Sell it to the ASC's surgeon-owners and administrator, not to health-system finance, since that is where the enterprise tools don't sell. Go through ASCA chapters and ASC management companies.
4. Make the durable product a pre-bill gate. Before the claim goes out, it checks that the invoice is attached and that the L8699 or 027x line is coded to trigger the carve-out. Contingency recovery is the wedge and prospective monitoring is the recurring revenue.
5. Build channel deals with the ASC billing vendors and ASC software vendors (SIS, HST, Nimble). Offer them a white-label carve-out audit rather than competing head-on.

Before building, run the 3-5 free lookbacks to test whether the leakage is real. If ASC-specialist billers already capture most carve-outs, the market shrinks to poorly billed ASCs and small hospitals. Then re-run the competitor check with live WebSearch (Cloudmed/R1, Experian, small implant-billing consultancies, YC and Crunchbase), which this pass could not do.
